question: The case of Tayeb Benabderrahmane

Mr Tayeb Benabderrahmane, a French national, was sentenced to death in absentia in Qatar in May 2023 following a secret, blatantly unfair trial. In its Opinion No 28/2025, adopted on 8 April 2025, the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention concluded that he had been arbitrarily detained, tortured and stripped of his right to a fair trial.

The UN called on Qatar to open an independent investigation, prosecute those responsible and compensate the victim. These conclusions are extremely grave and call for a firm EU response. What is at stake here is not only the protection of an EU citizen – the victim of a flagrant human rights violation – but also the EU’s credibility as a global player committed to upholding international law. 1.
What action does the VP/HR intend to take with the Qatari authorities to ensure that the UN Working Group’s recommendations concerning Mr Tayeb Benabderrahmane are acted on swiftly and effectively?
Does the VP/HR intend to make the EU's economic and political relations with Qatar conditional on the upholding of fundamental rights and proper adherence to the UN recommendations?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.11.2025) The EU is following the case and is concerned about the findings of the United Nations (UN) Working Group on Arbitrary Detention in its Opinion No 28/2025, which concluded that the person mentioned in the subject of the question had been arbitrarily detained, subjected to illtreatment and denied the right to a fair trial.

The EU consistently calls on all partners, including Qatar, to respect international human rights obligations and to implement in good faith the recommendations of UN human rights mechanisms. The EU Delegation in Doha, in coordination with the French authorities, follows the case and raises its concerns with the Qatari authorities, including in the framework of the regular political and human rights dialogues.

The EU Special Representative for Human Rights also engages actively with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries on individual cases of political prisoners. Human rights and the rule of law are central to the EU’s external action and shape its relations with Qatar and the GCC states.

Such issues were also discussed at the first EU-GCC Summit in Brussels on 16 October 2024, where both sides reaffirmed their commitment to deepening cooperation on human rights as a key pillar of their partnership.
